AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Pest and Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Pest and Disease Control.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Poultry Rearing in a Fold? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Poultry Rearing in a Fold.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Poultry Rearing in a Fold.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Poultry Rearing in a Fold.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Poultry Rearing in a Fold.

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

7. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Kitchen and Backyard Gardening? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Kitchen and Backyard Gardening.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Kitchen and Backyard Gardening.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Kitchen and Backyard Gardening.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Kitchen and Backyard Gardening.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Harvesting and Storage? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Harvesting and Storage.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water Harvesting and Storage.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Harvesting and Storage.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Harvesting and Storage.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparation of Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparation of Animal Products.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Preparation of Animal Products.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparation of Animal Products.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparation of Animal Products.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Conservation Measures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Conservation Measures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Conservation Measures.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Conservation Measures.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Soil Conservation Measures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Water Harvesting and Storage and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Kitchen and Backyard Gardening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Poultry Rearing in a Fold and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Pest and Disease Control.

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Poultry Rearing in a Fold.

5. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

6. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

7. B — Producers

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Kitchen and Backyard Gardening.

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Harvesting and Storage.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparation of Animal Products.

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Poultry Rearing in a Fold; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
